sections.h2: Which office handles Westland property tax?
sections.html:
Westland runs its own tax collection through the Finance Department at City Hall, 36300 Warren Road, 48185. By charter the Finance Director is also the city's Treasurer. The city lies in Wayne County, and the county treasurer takes over any real property bill the city has not collected.

Call 734-467-3172 for tax billing or 734-467-3169 for Finance. City Hall staff are in from 9 am to 5 pm on weekdays. Values come from the Assessor's Office at the same address, phone 734-467-3160, which promises an answer within a business day.

Deeds are a different matter. They are filed with the Wayne County Register of Deeds in downtown Detroit and never at City Hall.

Bills leave the city on July 1 and December 1. Payment is expected by August 15 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter one, moving to the next business day if the date lands on a weekend, unless Council grants more time.

Extensions are not rare. Council has set a later no-penalty deadline for summer in some years, and it votes on each one separately. Check the city's website for a notice before counting on the printed date, and phone 734-467-3172 if a bill never arrives.

A summer deferral is available by application. The city's online form is returned to the Tax Clerk by email, by mail to City Hall, or in the drop box.

Options are the city's online payment portal, a phone service, and City Hall itself. Fees depend on the route.

  • The Point and Pay phone line, 844-400-3556, adds a 3% service fee.
  • Counter payments are made at City Hall in business hours.
  • Two drop boxes accept checks, money orders and cashier's checks, never cash, and the items go in a sealed envelope.
  • The white box beside the postal mailbox at the northeast edge of the lot needs no stamp. A slot in the wall just east of the main door is the other.

If you sell near a due date, ask the title company to settle the bill from proceeds and keep the receipt. The billing line can give the parcel's balance.

sections.h2: How is a Westland home valued for tax?
sections.html:
Each year the Assessor sets a value for every parcel at 50% of true cash value as of December 31, the level state law requires. The bill itself multiplies taxable value, a different figure from assessed value, by the local millage rates, so a voter-approved millage change moves the bill even if the assessment holds still.

Three appraisal methods are in use. Sales comparison looks at comparable homes that sold. The income method fits rentals. The 2026 assessments rely on sales from April 2023 through March 2025 and set aside bank sales and foreclosures as non-arm's-length deals.

A sale price cannot by itself justify a change. Neither the Assessor nor the Board of Review may raise or lower a value on price alone. The city posts its economic condition factor and land value studies, and an online lookup shows taxable value, balance owed, a parcel map and the legal description.

The March Board of Review is the route, and it is the only time of year a residential value can be appealed. Notices arrive near the end of February, roughly two weeks before the board first sits, with hearing dates printed on them.

  • File a Petition to the Board of Review for every parcel, since incomplete ones are returned.
  • Appointments open only after notices are mailed and run five minutes each. A letter is allowed as an alternative.
  • Back your claim with an appraisal, comparable sales, a market analysis or photographs. Appointments and letters count equally, and the board decides later from the paper record.
  • Submit everything by 1:00 pm on the final scheduled meeting day.
  • A lawyer, accountant or agent may appear if both of you sign a written authorization.

Three members and two alternates serve, chosen by the Mayor and confirmed by Council. The board organizes on the Tuesday after the first Monday in March in the Council Chambers. It hears challenges to assessed value, hardship exemptions under MCL 211.7u and classification disputes, and fixes clerical errors and mutual mistakes of fact.

sections.h2: What if the tax stays unpaid?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Treasurer, at 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit, takes over. A bill still open at the local office after the last day of February turns delinquent on March 1 and can be paid only to the county from then on.

The county's timeline is blunt. A year of delinquency means forfeiture the following March 1, monthly interest moving from 1% to 1.5% back to the start, plus $175 for foreclosure and $30 for recording. At least ten written notices go out first, payment plans exist, and parcels that are foreclosed are offered to public bodies and then auctioned in September and October.

A seller with a balance can usually pay it from sale proceeds. Interest accrues monthly, so get a payoff figure from the Wayne County Treasurer before closing.

sections.h2: What the buyer and seller file after closing
sections.html:
MCL 211.27a gives the buyer 45 days to tell the assessing office about the transfer on the state's form, showing the parties, the date, the real price and the parcel number. Title companies commonly hand out the form at closing.

Taxable value is limited while one owner holds the home and then resets toward assessed value the year after a transfer, so the next owner's first bill can run well above yours. Anyone who claimed the principal residence exemption should file the state's rescind form for the property sold. Ask the Westland Assessor's Office for current forms and the status of your exemption.

Westland is a Detroit suburb roughly 18 miles west of downtown, covering 20.43 square miles of land. The Norwayne subdivision, put up for returning soldiers who worked in nearby plants, is among its oldest neighborhoods.

School assignments vary by street. Wayne-Westland Community Schools serve most of the city. The northern edge belongs to Livonia Public Schools, and small southern pockets are in Taylor and Romulus districts.

The city has 82,333 residents and 35,932 households of about 2.30 people. Housing is 61.3% owner-occupied, with a middle home value of $184,600 and median gross rent of $1,158. Median household income is $62,076.

faqs.q: When do Westland summer and winter taxes come due?
faqs.a: August 15 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter bill, after bills mailed July 1 and December 1. Council may extend either, so check the city's website for a notice.

faqs.q: What number reaches Westland tax billing?
faqs.a: 734-467-3172, answered Monday through Friday from 9 am to 5 pm at City Hall, 36300 Warren Road. The Finance Department is at 734-467-3169.

faqs.q: What is the window for a Westland assessment appeal?
faqs.a: March. Notices come near the end of February with hearing dates. You file a petition for each parcel, schedule an appointment or write a letter, and attach evidence such as an appraisal or comparable sales.

faqs.q: Does Westland charge extra to pay taxes by phone?
faqs.a: Yes, the Point and Pay line at 844-400-3556 adds a 3% service fee. Payments at the City Hall counter or in the drop boxes by check or money order carry no listed fee.

faqs.q: Where is Westland tax paid once it is delinquent?
faqs.a: At the Wayne County Treasurer, 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit. A bill unpaid at the end of February becomes delinquent on March 1 and the county alone accepts payment after that.
